sections.heading: Current MOD evidence baseline
items: The current bounded corpus contains 38 unique MOD resources, 166 objects, 180 meshes, 20,976 vertices and 285 transforms across em000, pl000 main/cloth-associated resources and id100, so the public page no longer treats enemy-only observations as the whole format population.

The canonical MOD adapter retains the recovered 0x40 document header, 0x40 outer-object and 0x50 inner-mesh grammar together with position, normal, fixed-point UV, BLENDINDICES and packed skin/topology streams, node-domain hierarchy, world transforms and texture-companion relationships.

Unknown source bytes remain preservation authority: zero-heavy fields are not silently promoted to padding, and shared offsets across MOD, EFM and SCM are not assigned the same semantic without independent executable evidence.

sections.heading: Important 2026-09-09 closures and corrections
items: BLENDINDICES.x is now bounded by the canonical runtime/shader chain: compiled DXBC input signatures use ReadWriteMask 0xE and therefore consume Y/Z/W rather than X; the raw X byte is still part of the serialized ABI and must be preserved rather than treated as disposable padding.

Object source flag 0x00100000 has an EXE-confirmed technical renderer semantic: in the active low-mode path it switches legacy GS TEST_1 AREF between 0 and 16 and ZBUF_1.ZMSK between masked and writable depth state. This does not authorize an invented artistic label such as cloth or transparent material.

The older universal decimal interpretation of MOD header +0x14 is rejected by the expanded pl000/id100 corpus. The field is a raw runtime-carried u32 transferred to manager +0xE4 and remains PRESERVED_UNDECODED at the high-level semantic layer.

Mesh +0x38 is family-sensitive rather than globally equivalent: the audited MOD path does not forward the slot while the homologous EFM path uses it for COLOR0-facing state. Mesh +0x0C/+0x4C and transform +0x1C also retain source-preservation contracts without being renamed as padding.

sections.heading: What MOD still does not authorize
items: Source flag 0x00200000 is confirmed as baseline/effective runtime-carried state, but its distinct terminal semantic consumer remains unresolved and it must not inherit semantics from unrelated equal-mask manager/object fields.

Reader, hierarchy, skinning, topology and renderer-state recovery do not authorize unrestricted MOD writing: mutation dependencies, deterministic authoring layout, reopen/reparse, container reintegration, original-game acceptance and rollback integrity remain separate promotion gates.

A visible skeleton, decoded skin weights, a correctly rendered model or a zero-filled corpus field is not proof that every semantic, variant or writer rule is known. Public claims therefore stay evidence-bounded rather than advertising 100% reverse or arbitrary original-game-safe editing.

lessons.title: 01 — What is MOD?
lessons.description: Start with the role of MOD in DMC3 HD, its evidence boundaries and the difference between a model document, its runtime objects and neighboring resource families.

lessons.title: 02 — Document, objects and meshes
lessons.description: Walk through the current multi-corpus document/object/mesh contract, corrected header +0x14 boundary, object flags and preserved mesh fields.

lessons.title: 03 — Skeleton, hierarchy and transforms
lessons.description: Study parent/order topology, local/world transforms and the executable-backed preservation boundary for transform +0x1C.

lessons.title: 04 — Skinning, topology and shader inputs
lessons.description: Follow packed influences and topology generation through the shader ABI, including the new compiled-DXBC closure showing BLENDINDICES Y/Z/W consumption but not X.

lessons.title: 05 — Textures and materials
lessons.description: Relate texture slots and companions to runtime material state and the EXE-confirmed 0x00100000 GS TEST_1/ZBUF_1 selector without inventing an artistic category.

lessons.title: 06 — Animation and motion groups
lessons.description: Understand the recovered motion-group table, node-domain animation relationships and the boundary where MOT evaluation becomes a separate authority.

lessons.title: 07 — Related formats
lessons.description: Compare MOD with SCM, SHW, EFM, MOT, SO and texture companions so shared physical concepts are not mistaken for identical semantics.

lessons.title: 08 — Evidence and unknowns
lessons.description: Review the expanded multi-corpus closure, rejected hypotheses, negative executable evidence and exact preservation rules for still-undecoded fields.

lessons.title: 09 — Reverse workflow
lessons.description: Use the project evidence workflow to move from raw bytes and corpus observations through hypotheses, implementation, tests and promotion gates.

lessons.title: 10 — Exercises and debugging
lessons.description: Practice diagnosing offsets, counts, hierarchy relationships, transform mistakes and skin/topology problems using evidence rather than visual guesswork.

lessons.title: MOD glossary
lessons.description: Reference current MOD terminology including runtime_metadata_u32, GS state selectors, BLENDINDICES.x evidence and preserved-undecoded boundaries.

lessons.title: MOD reference map
lessons.description: Jump from the latest public learning concepts to canonical code, tests, research notes and 2026-09-09 evidence packets.
